questions.text: जब साझेदारों की पूँजी परिवर्तनशील होती हैं, तब आहरण, आहरण पर ब्याज, पूँजी पर ब्याज, साझेदारों के वेतन, आदि के समायोजन ______ दर्शाए जाते हैं।
questions.text_english: When capitals of the partners are fluctuating, then the adjustments for drawings, interest on drawings, interest on capital, partners' salary, etc. are shown in the ______
questions.solution: Option B is correct because under the fluctuating capital method, all partner-related transactions and adjustments, such as drawings, salary, and interest on capital, are recorded directly in the Capital Accounts of the respective partners.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है क्योंकि परिवर्तनशील पूँजी पद्धति के अंतर्गत साझेदारों से संबंधित सभी समायोजन जैसे आहरण, पूँजी पर ब्याज, और वेतन सीधे साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते में ही दर्ज किए जाते हैं।

questions.text: निगम लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 40,000, 11% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन एक निश्चित बट्टे की दर पर किया । ऋणपत्रों का शोधन 20% प्रीमियम पर किया जाना था । इन ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन से पूर्व प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम का विद्यमान शेष ₹ 13,00,000 था। 'ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर हानि' को अपलिखित करने के पश्चात्, प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम का शेष ₹ 3,00,000 था। उपर्युक्त ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन किया गया था :
questions.text_english: Nigam Ltd. issued 40,000, 11% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at a certain rate of discount. The debentures were to be redeemed at 20% premium. Existing balance of Securities Premium before issue of these debentures was ₹ 13,00,000. After writing off 'Loss on issue of debentures', the balance in Securities Premium was ₹ 3,00,000. The above debentures were issued at a discount of:
questions.solution: Option D is correct because the total loss written off from Securities Premium is ten lakh rupees. This loss includes the premium on redemption, which is eight lakh rupees. The remaining two lakh rupees represent the discount on the issue. Calculating two lakh rupees over the total face value of forty lakh rupees yields a discount rate of five percent.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है क्योंकि प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम से अपलिखित कुल हानि दस लाख रुपये है। इस हानि में आठ लाख रुपये का शोधन पर प्रीमियम शामिल है, इसलिए निर्गमन पर बट्टा दो लाख रुपये है। 40,00,000 रुपये के अंकित मूल्य पर 2,00,000 रुपये का बट्टा 5% होता है।

questions.text: 31 मार्च, 2025 को, हरी तथा ओम के बीच साझेदारी का विघटन हो गया। हरी को विघटन कार्य की देखरेख के लिए नियुक्त किया गया जिसके लिए उसे ₹ 9,700 कमीशन दिया जाना था। वह विघटन व्ययों को वहन करने के लिए सहमत हो गया। विघटन के वास्तविक व्यय ₹ 8,900 थे जिनका भुगतान हरी के मित्र भानु ने उसकी तरफ से किया। वसूली खाते में डेबिट की गई राशि होगी :
questions.text_english: On 31st March, 2025, the partnership between Hari and Om was dissolved. Hari was appointed to look after dissolution work for which he was allowed a commission of ₹ 9,700. He agreed to bear the dissolution expenses. The actual expenses of dissolution amounted to ₹ 8,900 which were paid by Hari's friend, Bhanu on his behalf. The amount debited to Realisation Account will be :
questions.solution: Option A is correct because the Realisation Account is only debited with the agreed remuneration or commission payable to the partner for overseeing the dissolution. Since Hari agreed to personally bear the actual dissolution expenses, the firm's records are unaffected by his private settlement with Bhanu.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प A सही है क्योंकि वसूली खाते को केवल साझेदार को देय पारिश्रमिक या कमीशन के लिए डेबिट किया जाता है। चूँकि हरी ने स्वयं व्यय वहन करने की सहमति दी थी, इसलिए उसके मित्र द्वारा किए गए वास्तविक भुगतान का फर्म की पुस्तकों से कोई संबंध नहीं है।

questions.text: अतुल और निशा एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 4 : 1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। उनकी पूँजी क्रमश: ₹ 1,20,000 तथा ₹ 90,000 थीं। 1 अप्रैल, 2025 को, भविष्य के लाभों में 1/4 भाग के लिए उन्होंने मोना को एक नए साझेदार के रूप में फर्म में प्रवेश दिया। मोना अपनी पूँजी के रूप में ₹ 1,00,000 लाई। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्य था :
questions.text_english: Atul and Nisha were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4: 1. Their capitals were ₹ 1,20,000 and ₹ 90,000 respectively. On 1st April, 2025, they admitted Mona as a new partner in the firm for 1/4th share in the future profits. Mona brought ₹ 1,00,000 as her capital. The value of goodwill of the firm was:
questions.solution: Option C is correct because the total capitalized value of the firm based on Mona's share is four lakh rupees. Deducting the actual combined capital of all partners, which is three lakh ten thousand rupees, leaves a hidden goodwill balance of exactly ninety thousand rupees.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प C सही है क्योंकि मोना के हिस्से के आधार पर फर्म की कुल पूँजी चार लाख रुपये होती है। सभी साझेदारों की वास्तविक संयुक्त पूँजी (1,20,000 + 90,000 + 1,00,000) को घटाने पर गुप्त ख्याति नब्बे हज़ार रुपये प्राप्त होती है।

questions.text: यशोदा तथा देवी एक फर्म की साझेदार थीं तथा 3 : 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटती थीं । 31 मार्च, 2025 को, उनका स्थिति विवरण ₹20,00,000 का भूमि एवं भवन तथा ₹ 6,00,000 का फर्नीचर दर्शा रहा था। इस तिथि को भविष्य के लाभों में 1/4 भाग के लिए उन्होंने पूनम को एक नए साझेदार के रूप में फर्म में प्रवेश दिया। पूनम के प्रवेश पर, यह पाया गया कि भूमि एवं भवन का मूल्यांकन 20% कम है। पूनम के प्रवेश पर, पुनर्मूल्यांकन खाते को :
questions.text_english: Yashoda and Devi were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3: 2. On 31st March, 2025, their balance sheet showed land and building at ₹ 20,00,000 and furniture at ₹ 6,00,000. On that date they admitted Poonam as a new partner for 1/4th share in the future profits of the firm. On Poonam's admission, it was found that land and building is undervalued by 20%. On Poonam's admission, Revaluation Account will be:
questions.solution: Option D is correct because an asset undervalued by twenty percent means the recorded twenty lakh rupees represents eighty percent of the actual value. The true value is twenty-five lakhs, meaning there is an increase of five lakhs, which must be credited to the Revaluation Account as a gain.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प D सही है क्योंकि यदि 20,00,000 रुपये 20% कम मूल्यांकन (80%) को दर्शाते हैं, तो वास्तविक मूल्य 25,00,000 रुपये है। 5,00,000 रुपये की इस वृद्धि को फर्म के लिए लाभ मानते हुए पुनर्मूल्यांकन खाते में क्रेडिट किया जाएगा।

questions.text: दिव्या तथा भोली एक फर्म की साझेदार थीं तथा 3 : 1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटती थीं । 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को, उनकी स्थायी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 8,00,000 तथा ₹ 6,00,000 थीं । 30 सितम्बर, 2024 को, भोली ने ₹ 50,000 की अतिरिक्त पूँजी लगाई। साझेदारी संलेख में पूँजी पर 12% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज देने का प्रावधान था। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए भोली की पूँजी पर ब्याज की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Divya and Bholi were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3: 1. On 1st April, 2024, their fixed capitals were ₹ 8,00,000 and ₹ 6,00,000 respectively. On 30th September, 2024, Bholi introduced ₹ 50,000 as additional capital. Partnership deed provided that interest on capital will be allowed @ 12% p.a. Interest on Bholi's capital for the year ended 31st March, 2025 was:
questions.solution: Option B is correct because the interest is computed in two parts. A full year's interest on the opening balance of six lakhs at twelve percent equals seventy-two thousand rupees. The additional capital of fifty thousand rupees earns twelve percent interest for six months, which is three thousand rupees. The total interest is thus seventy-five thousand rupees.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है क्योंकि ब्याज की गणना दो भागों में की जाती है। प्रारंभिक शेष ₹ 6,00,000 पर 12% की दर से पूरे वर्ष का ब्याज ₹ 72,000 होता है। 30 सितंबर को लगाई गई अतिरिक्त पूँजी ₹ 50,000 पर 12% की दर से 6 महीने का ब्याज ₹ 3,000 होता है। इस प्रकार कुल ब्याज ₹ 75,000 होगा।

sub_questions.text_english: Anup, Bharti and Manoj were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 11:8: 1. From 1st April, 2025, they decided to share the future profits in the ratio of 2:2: 1. The gain or sacrifice of each partner due to change in profit sharing ratio will be:

options.A: अनूप का अभिलाभ 3/20, मनोज का त्याग 3/20
options.B: अनूप का त्याग 3/20, मनोज का अभिलाभ 3/20
options.C: अनूप का अभिलाभ 3/20, मनोज का अभिलाभ 3/20
options.D: अनूप का त्याग 3/20, मनोज का त्याग 3/20

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct because deducting the new share from the old share yields the result. Anup's old share is eleven over twenty and his new is eight over twenty, showing a sacrifice of three over twenty. Manoj's old is one over twenty and new is four over twenty, indicating a gain of three over twenty.

sub_questions.text: अरुण, वरुण तथा तरुण एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। 31 मार्च, 2025 को, अरुण की मृत्यु हो गई। वरुण तथा तरुण ने भविष्य में लाभों को बराबर-बराबर बाँटने का निर्णय किया। वरुण तथा तरुण का अभिलाभ अनुपात होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Arun, Varun and Tarun were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. On 31st March, 2025, Arun died. Varun and Tarun decided to share future profits equally. The gaining ratio of Varun and Tarun will be :
sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct because the gaining ratio is derived by subtracting the old share from the new share. Varun gains the difference between one-half and three-tenths, which is two-tenths. Tarun gains the difference between one-half and two-tenths, which is three-tenths, giving a ratio of two to three.

sub_questions.text_english: Atul, Bajaj and Madan were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 1: 2: 5. The partnership deed provides that interest on a partner's drawings shall be charged @ 18% per annum. During the year ended 31st March, 2025, Bajaj withdrew ₹ 7,000 at the end of each quarter. Interest on Bajaj's drawings will be :
sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct because the total drawings amount to twenty-eight thousand rupees for the year. Since drawings are made at the end of each quarter, the average period is four point five months, making the interest eighteen percent of twenty-eight thousand for four point five months, which is one thousand eight hundred ninety.

sub_questions.text: दामोदर, राव तथा श्रीधरन एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 3 : 1 : 1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। उनकी स्थायी पूँजी क्रमश: ₹ 4,00,000; ₹3,00,000 तथा ₹ 2,00,000 थीं। पूँजी पर 6% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज देय था। राव की पूँजी पर ब्याज देने की रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि होगी :

Their fixed capitals were ₹ 4,00,000; ₹ 3,00,000 and ₹ 2,00,000 respectively. Interest on capital is allowed at the rate of 6% per annum. Journal entry for allowing interest on Rao's capital will be :

options.A: लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाता नाम 18,000; राव का पूँजी खाता जमा 18,000
options.B: लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाता नाम 18,000; राव का चालू खाता जमा 18,000

options_english.C: Interest on Capital A/c Dr. 18,000; To Rao's Current A/c 18,000
options_english.D: Interest on Capital A/c Dr. 18,000; To Rao's Capital A/c 18,000

(i) पूँजी पर 9% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज
(ii) उसकी मृत्यु की तिथि तक फर्म के लाभों में उसका भाग
30 सितंबर, 2025 तक तनवी ने अपने व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए ₹ 1,00,000 का आहरण किया और 12% वार्षिक दर से आहरण पर ब्याज प्रभारित किया जाएगा। फर्म के लाभों में उसके भाग की गणना पिछले वर्ष के लाभ के आधार पर की गई। पिछले वर्ष का लाभ ₹ 3,60,000 था। तनवी के कानूनी प्रतिनिधियों को प्रस्तुत करने के लिए उसका पूँजी खाता तैयार कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Tanvi, Manvi and Noori were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3: 2. On 1st April, 2025, their capitals were ₹ 8,00,000; ₹ 6,00,000 and ₹ 4,00,000 respectively. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. Tanvi died on 30th September, 2025. The partnership deed provides that in the event of death of a partner, his/her legal representatives will be entitled to the following:
(i) Interest on capital @ 9% p.a.
(ii) Her share in the profits of the firm till the date of her death.
Till 30th September, 2025 Tanvi had withdrawn ₹ 1,00,000 for personal use and interest on drawings @ 12% p.a. is to be charged. Her share in the profits of the firm was calculated on the basis of last year's profit. Last year's profit amounted to ₹ 3,60,000. Prepare Tanvi's Capital Account to be presented to her legal representatives.

key_points: Credit side: Opening Capital ₹ 8,00,000
Credit side: Interest on capital ₹ 36,000
Credit side: P&L Suspense (Profit share) ₹ 90,000
Debit side: Drawings ₹ 1,00,000
Debit side: Interest on drawings ₹ 3,000 (avg 3 months)
Final amount to Executors: ₹ 8,23,000

questions.solution: In Tanvi's Capital Account, the credit side records her opening capital of eight lakh rupees. Interest on capital for six months at nine percent amounts to thirty-six thousand rupees. Her share of profit is calculated as three lakh sixty thousand rupees multiplied by her five-tenths share for six months, yielding ninety thousand rupees, which is credited via Profit & Loss Suspense. On the debit side, her drawings of one lakh rupees are recorded. The interest on drawings at twelve percent for an average period of three months comes to three thousand rupees. The final balancing figure transferred to Tanvi's Executors Account is eight lakh twenty-three thousand rupees.

The ten thousand rupees deficiency is entirely borne by Sukesh. Sukesh's normal share of two lakh seventy-five thousand rupees is reduced by this ten thousand, leaving him with a final profit transfer of two lakh sixty-five thousand rupees. sub_questions.text: ओएसिस लिमिटेड ने ₹ 15,30,000 के क्रय प्रतिफल के बदले नितारा लिमिटेड से ₹ 12,00,000 मूल्य का भवन, ₹ 1,90,000 मूल्य की मशीनरी तथा ₹ 3,00,000 मूल्य का फर्नीचर क्रय किया तथा इसकी ₹ 90,000 की देयताओं को लिया। ओएसिस लिमिटेड ने क्रय प्रतिफल का भुगतान ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 11% ऋणपत्रों को 10% बट्टे पर निर्गमित करके किया। उपर्युक्त लेनदेनों के लिए ओएसिस लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Oasis Ltd. purchased building worth ₹ 12,00,000, machinery worth ₹ 1,90,000 and furniture worth ₹ 3,00,000 from Nitara Ltd. and took over its liabilities of ₹ 90,000 for a purchase consideration of ₹ 15,30,000. Oasis Ltd. paid the purchase consideration by issuing 11% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 10%. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Oasis Ltd. for the above transactions.

key_points: Record asset and liability acquisition with Capital Reserve
Calculate number of debentures issued
Record issue of debentures at discount

sub_questions.solution: To record the purchase, the firm must first debit Building Account for twelve lakhs, Machinery Account for one lakh ninety thousand, and Furniture Account for three lakhs, while crediting Liabilities for ninety thousand and Nitara Limited for the fifteen lakh thirty thousand purchase consideration. The remaining balancing figure of seventy thousand rupees is credited to Capital Reserve. For the payment, the issue price per debenture is ninety rupees, meaning seventeen thousand debentures are issued. The final entry debits Nitara Limited with fifteen lakh thirty thousand, debits Discount on Issue of Debentures with one lakh seventy thousand, and credits the eleven percent Debentures Account with the total face value of seventeen lakh rupees.

sub_questions.text: 1 अप्रैल, 2025 को, भारत हैवी इंडस्ट्रीज़ लिमिटेड ने ₹ 15,00,000 के क्रय प्रतिफल के बदले मैक लिमिटेड के चालू व्यवसाय का क्रय किया जिसमें ₹ 20,00,000 पुस्तक मूल्य की विविध परिसम्पत्तियाँ तथा ₹ 8,00,000 की विविध देयताएँ सम्मिलित थीं। क्रय प्रतिफल का भुगतान ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 8,000, 9% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 25% प्रीमियम पर करके तथा शेष को मैक लिमिटेड के पक्ष में बैंक ड्राफ्ट द्वारा भुगतान करके किया। भारत हैवी इंडस्ट्रीज़ लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में उपर्युक्त लेनदेनों के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: On 1st April, 2025, Bharat Heavy Industries Ltd. purchased the running business of Mac Ltd. consisting of sundry assets of the book value of ₹ 20,00,000 and sundry liabilities of ₹ 8,00,000 for a purchase consideration of ₹ 15,00,000. The purchase consideration was paid by issuing 8,000, 9% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at a premium of 25% and the balance was paid by a bank draft in favour of Mac Ltd. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of Bharat Heavy Industries Ltd.

key_points: Record asset and liability acquisition with Goodwill
Record debenture issue at premium
Record balance bank draft payment

sub_questions.solution: The initial journal entry records the acquisition by debiting Sundry Assets Account with twenty lakhs and debiting Goodwill Account with three lakhs as a balancing figure, while crediting Sundry Liabilities Account with eight lakhs and Mac Limited with fifteen lakhs for the purchase consideration. To settle the purchase consideration, Mac Limited is debited with fifteen lakhs. In exchange, the nine percent Debentures Account is credited with the eight lakh face value of the debentures, the Securities Premium Account is credited with two lakh rupees representing the premium, and the remaining five lakh rupees is credited to the Bank Account reflecting the bank draft payment.

रीटा और मोहित एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 7: 3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । उनकी पूँजी क्रमश: ₹ 7,00,000 तथा ₹ 3,00,000 थीं। प्रत्याय की सामान्य दर 10% थी। पिछले चार वर्षों के लाभ थे : 
2021-22 ₹3,30,000
2022-23 ₹4,00,000
2023-24 (₹70,000)
2024-25 ₹5,00,000
वर्ष 2024 – 25 के अंतिम स्टॉक का मूल्यांकन ₹ 40,000 से कम किया गया। ख्याति का मूल्यांकन पिछले चार वर्षों के औसत अधिलाभों के दो वर्षों के क्रय के आधार पर किया जाएगा। फर्म की ख्याति के मूल्य की गणना कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Rita and Mohit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 7: 3. Their capitals were ₹7,00,000 and ₹ 3,00,000 respectively. The normal rate of return was 10%. The profits for the last four years were :
2021-22 ₹3,30,000
2022-23 ₹4,00,000
2023-24 (₹70,000)
2024-25 ₹5,00,000
The closing stock for the year 2024-25 was undervalued by ₹ 40,000. Goodwill is to be valued at two years' purchase of last four years' average super profits. Calculate the value of goodwill of the firm.

key_points: Calculate Capital Employed and Normal Profit
Adjust profits for undervalued closing stock
Calculate Average Profit and Super Profit
Calculate final Goodwill

questions.image_description: A table showing profits/losses for four consecutive years.
questions.solution: The firm's capital employed is the sum of both partners' capitals, which equals ten lakh rupees. The normal profit calculated at a ten percent return on this capital yields one lakh rupees. The total profit must be adjusted by adding back the forty thousand rupees undervaluation of closing stock for the year 2024-25. The adjusted sum of profits over the four years equals twelve lakh rupees, producing an average profit of three lakh rupees. The super profit is the difference of two lakh rupees between the average and normal profit. Finally, the goodwill is calculated as two years' purchase of the super profit, giving a final value of four lakh rupees.

(i) एबी लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 30,000, 10% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 5% प्रीमियम पर किया, जिनका शोधन 10% प्रीमियम पर किया जाएगा।
(ii) सीडी लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 40,000, 8% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन सममूल्य पर किया, जिनका शोधन 10% प्रीमियम पर किया जाएगा।
questions.text_english:
Pass necessary journal entries for issue of debentures for the following transactions
(i) AB Ltd. issued 30,000, 10% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at a premium of 5%, redeemable at a premium of 10%.
(ii) CD Ltd. issued 40,000, 8% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at par, redeemable at a premium of 10%.

key_points: Record receipt and allotment for AB Ltd. incorporating premium and loss
Record receipt and allotment for CD Ltd. incorporating loss on issue

questions.solution: For AB Limited, the first journal entry debits Bank Account and credits Debenture Application and Allotment Account with thirty-one lakh fifty thousand rupees, capturing the face value plus a five percent issue premium. The allotment entry debits Debenture Application and Allotment Account with thirty-one lakh fifty thousand, and debits Loss on Issue of Debentures Account with three lakhs for the redemption premium. It then credits the ten percent Debentures Account with the thirty lakh face value, Securities Premium Account with one lakh fifty thousand, and Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account with three lakhs. For CD Limited, the first entry debits Bank Account and credits Debenture Application and Allotment Account with forty lakh rupees. The allotment entry debits Debenture Application and Allotment Account with forty lakhs, debits Loss on Issue of Debentures Account with four lakhs for the redemption premium, credits the eight percent Debentures Account with forty lakhs, and credits Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account with four lakhs.

questions.text:
नम्रता, भावी तथा सुरभी एक फर्म की साझेदार थीं तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटती थीं। 31 मार्च, 2025 को उनकी पूँजी क्रमश: ₹ 10,00,000; ₹ 8,00,000 तथा ₹ 6,00,000 थीं। 1 अप्रैल, 2025 से, उन्होंने भविष्य में लाभों को बराबर-बराबर बाँटने का निर्णय लिया। यह सहमति हुई कि लाभ विभाजन अनुपात में परिवर्तन पर :
(i) फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹2,40,000 किया जाएगा।
(ii) परिसम्पत्तियों तथा देयताओं का पुनर्मूल्यांकन किया जाएगा। परिसम्पत्तियों के पुनर्मूल्यांकन तथा देयताओं के पुनर्निर्धारण के परिणामस्वरूप ₹ 20,000 का लाभ हुआ।
(iii) पुनर्गठित फर्म की कुल पूँजी ₹ 30,00,000 होगी तथा वह साझेदारों के नए लाभ विभाजन अनुपात में होगी। इस उद्देश्य के लिए, जैसी भी स्थिति होगी, साझेदार आवश्यकतानुसार नगद लाएँगे अथवा उन्हें नगद भुगतान कर दिया जाएगा।
फर्म के पुनर्गठन पर साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते तैयार कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Namrata, Bhavi and Surbhi were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. On 31st March, 2025, their capitals were ₹10,00,000; ₹ 8,00,000 and ₹ 6,00,000 respectively. With effect from 1st April, 2025, they decided to share the future profits equally. It was agreed that on change in profit sharing ratio :
(i) Goodwill of the firm will be valued at ₹ 2,40,000.
(ii) Revaluation of assets and liabilities will be carried out. The revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities resulted in a gain of ₹ 20,000.
(iii) Total capital of the reconstituted firm will be ₹30,00,000 and the same will be in proportion of the new profit sharing ratio of the partners. For this purpose, necessary cash will be brought in by the partners or paid off to the partners, as the case may be.
Prepare Partners' Capital Accounts on the reconstitution of the firm.

key_points: Record opening capital balances
Distribute revaluation gain in old ratio
Pass goodwill adjustment entry
Calculate target capital balances
Record cash brought in or withdrawn to match target capital

questions.solution: In the Partners' Capital Accounts, the opening balances are credited first: ten lakhs for Namrata, eight lakhs for Bhavi, and six lakhs for Surbhi. The revaluation gain of twenty thousand rupees is distributed in the old ratio, crediting Namrata by ten thousand, Bhavi by six thousand, and Surbhi by four thousand. The goodwill adjustment involves finding the gaining and sacrificing ratios: Namrata sacrifices five-thirtieths, Bhavi gains one-thirtieth, and Surbhi gains four-thirtieths. Consequently, Namrata is credited forty thousand, Bhavi is debited eight thousand, and Surbhi is debited thirty-two thousand. The new target capital is ten lakhs for each partner. After adjusting the balances, Namrata has a surplus of fifty thousand which she withdraws via bank. Bhavi has a deficiency of two lakh two thousand, and Surbhi has a deficiency of four lakh twenty-eight thousand, both of which they must bring in via bank to correctly balance their capital accounts at ten lakhs each.

sub_questions.text_english:
Anand and Bir were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3: 2. On 31st March, 2025, their Balance Sheet was as follows:
...
On 1st April, 2025, they admitted Vishal as a new partner for 1/6th share in the profits of the firm. It was agreed that :
(i) Vishal will bring ₹ 45,000 as his capital and ₹ 15,000 for his share of goodwill premium.
(ii) Stock was to be reduced by 10% and machinery was to be appreciated by 10%.
(iii) Furniture was revalued at ₹ 27,000.
(iv) 5% provision for bad debts was to be created and ₹ 600 were to be provided for outstanding repair bill.
(v) There were unrecorded investments of ₹ 3,000 which were to be recorded.
(vi) A creditor of ₹ 900 was not likely to claim his money and hence was to be written off.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of the firm on Vishal's admission.

key_points: Record cash brought in for capital and premium
Distribute Premium for Goodwill to sacrificing partners
Record all revaluation gains and losses properly
Transfer net revaluation profit to old partners
Distribute Workmen Compensation Fund to old partners

sub_questions.solution: The first entry debits Cash with sixty thousand, crediting Vishal's Capital Account with forty-five thousand and Premium for Goodwill Account with fifteen thousand rupees. The fifteen thousand premium is then distributed in the sacrificing ratio of three to two, crediting Anand with nine thousand and Bir with six thousand. The revaluation losses are recorded by debiting Revaluation Account with nine thousand nine hundred, while crediting Stock with four thousand five hundred, Furniture with three thousand, Provision for Doubtful Debts with one thousand eight hundred, and Outstanding Repair Bill with six hundred. Gains are recorded by debiting Plant and Machinery with nine thousand, Unrecorded Investments with three thousand, and Creditors with nine hundred, crediting the Revaluation Account with twelve thousand nine hundred. The net revaluation profit of three thousand rupees is distributed to Anand and Bir as one thousand eight hundred and one thousand two hundred respectively. Finally, the fifteen thousand Workmen Compensation Fund is distributed to Anand and Bir, crediting their accounts with nine thousand and six thousand rupees respectively.

(iv) श्याम की सेवानिवृत्ति पर फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 6,00,000 था।

sub_questions.text_english:
Radha, Shyam and Meera were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2025 was as follows:
...
Shyam retired from the firm on the above date on the following terms:
(i) The new profit sharing ratio between the remaining partners was agreed at 3:2.
(ii) The value of stock was to be reduced by ₹ 1,20,000.
(iii) Patents were considered as valueless and hence were to be written off.
(iv) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 6,00,000 on Shyam's retirement.
(v) Shyam was paid ₹ 1,00,000 immediately on his retirement and the balance was transferred to his loan account.
Prepare Revaluation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts.

key_points: Prepare Revaluation Account calculating total loss
Distribute Revaluation loss equally
Adjust Goodwill utilizing the gaining ratio
Distribute General Reserve
Settle retiring partner's account via cash payment and loan transfer

sub_questions.solution: The Revaluation Account is debited with one lakh twenty thousand for the reduction in stock and one lakh eighty thousand for writing off the valueless patents. This creates a total revaluation loss of three lakh rupees, which is credited from the Revaluation Account and debited equally to all three partners' Capital Accounts at one lakh rupees each. For the goodwill adjustment, Shyam's share is two lakh rupees. Because the new ratio is three to two, Radha gains four-fifteenths and Meera gains one-fifteenth, so Radha's Capital Account is debited with one lakh sixty thousand and Meera's with forty thousand, crediting Shyam with two lakhs. The General Reserve of three lakhs is divided equally, crediting each partner with one lakh. Finally, Shyam's account shows a credit total of seven lakhs against a debit of one lakh, leaving six lakhs. He is paid one lakh immediately from the Bank, and the remaining five lakhs are securely transferred to his Loan Account.

sub_questions.text_english: Madhav Ltd. invited applications for issuing 4,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of ₹ 4 per share. The amount was payable as follows: On Application and Allotment: ₹ 6 per share (including premium ₹ 2), On First and Final Call - Balance. Applications for 6,00,000 shares were received. Applications for 1,00,000 shares were rejected and the application money was refunded. Shares were allotted on pro-rata basis to the remaining applicants. Excess money received on application and allotment was adjusted towards sums due on first and final call. A shareholder, who had applied for 500 shares, failed to pay the first and final call. His shares were forfeited. Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Madhav Ltd. for the above transactions.

key_points: Record application money received for 6,00,000 shares
Allocate application money transferring excess to Calls-in-Advance and Bank
Determine call amount due and adjust the Calls-in-Advance
Calculate unpaid call amount for the defaulting shareholder taking pro-rata excess into account
Record forfeiture of the defaulted shares

sub_questions.solution: The company first debits Bank Account and credits Share Application and Allotment Account with thirty-six lakh rupees for the six lakh applications received at six rupees each. Next, this money is allocated: Share Capital is credited with sixteen lakhs, Securities Premium with eight lakhs, Bank Account is credited with six lakhs for the rejected applications, and the remaining six lakh rupees is credited to Calls-in-Advance. When the First and Final Call of eight rupees per share becomes due, the total demanded is thirty-two lakh rupees. The shareholder who applied for five hundred shares was allotted four hundred shares based on the five-to-four pro-rata ratio. He had an excess of six hundred rupees carried forward, leaving an unpaid call amount of two thousand six hundred rupees out of his three thousand two hundred rupees call liability. The Bank Account receives twenty-five lakh ninety-seven thousand four hundred rupees after adjusting the advance and the arrears. Finally, the forfeiture entry debits Share Capital with four thousand rupees and Securities Premium with eight hundred rupees, while crediting Calls-in-Arrears with two thousand six hundred rupees and Share Forfeiture Account with two thousand two hundred rupees.

sub_questions.text_english: (i) NN Ltd. forfeited 800 equity shares of ₹ 100 each for non-payment of the first call of ₹ 20 per share. The second and final call of ₹ 30 per share was not yet made. Out of the forfeited shares, 600 shares were re-issued for ₹ 54,000 as fully paid-up. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of NN Ltd. (ii) KG Ltd. forfeited 7,000 equity shares of ₹ 100 each, issued at a premium of ₹ 20 per share, for non-payment of second and final call of ₹ 20 per share. The forfeited shares were re-issued at ₹ 80 per share, fully paid-up. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of KG Ltd.

key_points: Record forfeiture entry for NN Ltd. focusing on called-up capital
Record reissue entry and capital reserve transfer for NN Ltd.
Record forfeiture entry for KG Ltd. excluding premium received
Record reissue and capital reserve transfer for KG Ltd.

sub_questions.solution: For NN Limited, the first entry debits Equity Share Capital with fifty-six thousand rupees, representing seventy rupees called up on eight hundred shares. It credits Calls-in-Arrears with sixteen thousand and Share Forfeiture with forty thousand rupees. When six hundred shares are reissued for fifty-four thousand fully paid, the Bank Account is debited with fifty-four thousand, Share Forfeiture is debited with six thousand to cover the discount, and Share Capital is credited with sixty thousand. A capital reserve transfer entry then moves twenty-four thousand rupees from Share Forfeiture to Capital Reserve. For KG Limited, the forfeiture entry debits Equity Share Capital with seven lakh rupees for the seven thousand fully called shares, credits Calls-in-Arrears with one lakh forty thousand, and credits Share Forfeiture with five lakh sixty thousand rupees. Upon reissuing at eighty rupees per share, the Bank Account is debited with five lakh sixty thousand, Share Forfeiture is debited with one lakh forty thousand to cover the discount, and Share Capital is credited with seven lakhs. The final entry transfers the remaining balance of four lakh twenty thousand rupees from Share Forfeiture directly to Capital Reserve.

सोफिया तथा ललित एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि बराबर-बराबर बाँटते थे । 31 मार्च, 2025 को उनकी फर्म का विघटन हो गया। विविध परिसम्पत्तियों (रोकड़ हस्ते तथा बैंक में नगद को छोड़कर) तथा तृतीय पक्ष देयताओं को वसूली खाते में हस्तांतरित करने के पश्चात् निम्नलिखित लेनदेन हुए :

(v) ₹60,000 के लेनदारों को 5% बट्टे पर भुगतान किया गया।
(vi) ₹7,000 के वसूली व्ययों का भुगतान ललित द्वारा किया गया।

questions.text_english:
Sophia and Lalit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Their firm was dissolved on 31st March, 2025. After transferring sundry assets (other than cash in hand and cash at bank) and the third party liabilities to the Realisation Account, the following transactions took place:
(i) The firm had stock of the book value of ₹ 80,000. 50% of the stock was taken over by Sophia at 10% less than its book value and the remaining stock was sold at a gain of 15%.
(ii) There was an unrecorded investment which was sold for ₹ 25,000.
(iii) There were debtors of ₹ 1,20,000. Debtors realised 90% only and ₹ 5,000 were recovered for bad debts written off last year.
(iv) Sophia had given a loan to the firm of ₹ 52,000. She was paid ₹ 41,000 in full settlement of her claim.
(v) Creditors of ₹ 60,000 were paid at a discount of 5%.
(vi) Expenses of realisation amounting to ₹ 7,000 were paid by Lalit.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of the firm.

key_points: Record asset realizations including unrecorded assets and bad debt recovery
Record partner taking over an asset
Record settlement of partner's loan with gain transferred to Realisation
Record payment to creditors at discount
Record realisation expenses paid by a partner

questions.solution: In accounting for the dissolution, several journal entries must be recorded. First, Sophia's Capital Account is debited with thirty-six thousand rupees for taking over half the stock at a discount, crediting Realisation Account. Next, the Bank Account is debited with one lakh eighty-nine thousand rupees to capture the sale of the remaining stock for forty-six thousand, unrecorded investments for twenty-five thousand, and debtor realizations including bad debts recovered for one lakh eighteen thousand, with the corresponding credit given to the Realisation Account. To settle Sophia's loan of fifty-two thousand, Sophia's Loan Account is debited with the full amount, Bank Account is credited with forty-one thousand, and the Realisation Account is credited with the eleven thousand rupees gain on settlement. The payment of creditors debits the Realisation Account and credits the Bank Account with fifty-seven thousand rupees. Finally, for the expenses paid by Lalit, the Realisation Account is debited and Lalit's Capital Account is credited with seven thousand rupees.

...

key_points: Organize Base Year (2023-24) and Current Year (2024-25) columns correctly
Calculate Absolute Change and Percentage Change columns accurately
Compute Cost of Revenue, Total Expenses, Profit Before Tax, Tax, and Profit After Tax correctly for both years

questions.solution: The Comparative Statement of Profit and Loss structures the base year and current year sequentially to calculate both absolute and percentage changes. For the base year 2023-24, Revenue from Operations is forty lakh rupees. The Cost of Revenue is calculated at fifty percent, totaling twenty lakh rupees, and Other Expenses are ten lakh rupees, making the total expenses thirty lakh rupees. The Profit Before Tax is ten lakh rupees, and after a fifty percent tax deduction, the Profit After Tax is five lakh rupees. For the current year 2024-25, Revenue from Operations is sixty lakh rupees. The Cost of Revenue is thirty lakh rupees, and Other Expenses are fifteen lakh rupees, bringing total expenses to forty-five lakh rupees. The Profit Before Tax is fifteen lakh rupees, resulting in a Profit After Tax of seven lakh fifty thousand rupees. The percentage change effectively illustrates a fifty percent consistent increase across all comparable line items over the two periods.

key_points: Calculate Net Profit Before Tax
Calculate Interest on Long Term Debt
Determine Profit Before Interest and Tax (PBIT)
Apply formula for Interest Coverage Ratio

sub_questions.solution: The Interest Coverage Ratio demands the Net Profit Before Interest and Tax. The given Net Profit After Tax is two lakh forty thousand rupees, representing sixty percent of the pre-tax profit due to the forty percent tax rate. Grossing this up gives a Net Profit Before Tax of four lakh rupees. The interest on the eight percent long-term debt of ten lakh rupees amounts to eighty thousand rupees. Adding this interest to the pre-tax profit yields a Profit Before Interest and Tax of four lakh eighty thousand rupees. Dividing this four lakh eighty thousand by the interest expense of eighty thousand gives an Interest Coverage Ratio of precisely six times.

Opening inventory ₹2,00,000

Closing inventory was 2 times the opening inventory.

key_points: Calculate Cost of Revenue from Operations
Determine Closing Inventory
Compute Average Inventory
Apply formula for Inventory Turnover Ratio

sub_questions.solution: To calculate the Inventory Turnover Ratio, the Cost of Revenue from Operations must first be determined. Since Gross Profit is twenty-five percent of cost, Revenue from Operations represents one hundred and twenty-five percent of the cost. Therefore, the cost is fifteen lakhs multiplied by one hundred divided by one hundred twenty-five, equalling twelve lakh rupees. The Opening Inventory is given as two lakhs, and the Closing Inventory, being two times the opening, is four lakhs. Their sum is six lakhs, yielding an Average Inventory of three lakh rupees. Dividing the cost of twelve lakhs by the average inventory of three lakhs produces an Inventory Turnover Ratio of exactly four times.

JC Ltd. earned a net profit of ₹ 50,000 after providing depreciation of ₹ 20,000 on fixed assets and a transfer of ₹ 15,000 to general reserve. The position of its Current Assets and Current Liabilities was as follows:

key_points: Calculate Net Profit before Tax and Extraordinary Items
Adjust non-cash expenses like depreciation
Adjust working capital changes (Current Assets and Current Liabilities)
Determine final Cash Flow from Operating Activities

questions.solution: The process begins with the given net profit of fifty thousand rupees. To find the Net Profit before Tax and Extraordinary Items, the fifteen thousand transferred to the general reserve is added back, making it sixty-five thousand rupees. Non-cash expenses, specifically the depreciation of twenty thousand, are then added back to yield an Operating Profit before Working Capital Changes of eighty-five thousand rupees. Next, working capital adjustments are made. The increases in Trade Payables (ten thousand) and Expenses Payable (two thousand five hundred), along with the decrease in Prepaid Expenses (five thousand), are added, totaling seventeen thousand five hundred. Conversely, the increases in Trade Receivables (five thousand), Inventories (fifteen thousand), and Accrued Incomes (five thousand), along with the decrease in Income Received in Advance (five thousand), are subtracted, totaling thirty thousand. Integrating these adjustments, the final Cash Flow from Operating Activities equals seventy-two thousand five hundred rupees.

key_points: Define sequential codes: numbers or letters in consecutive order
Provide sequential code example
Define block codes: reserving ranges of numbers for specific categories

questions.solution: Sequential codes are systematic identifiers assigned in a continuous, uninterrupted numerical or alphabetical order. They are useful for tracking documents consecutively; for instance, sales invoices numbered 1001, 1002, and 1003. Block codes, however, involve reserving specific ranges or blocks of numbers exclusively for particular categories of items. This method allows for easy classification and expansion. For example, a company might allocate the 1000-1999 block entirely for its asset accounts, while reserving the 2000-2999 block strictly for its liability accounts.

questions.solution: While entering accounting data into vouchers, the transactions are primarily classified into three main categories for systematic processing. First are Receipt Vouchers, which strictly record any inflow or receipt of cash and bank balances. Second are Payment Vouchers, utilized exclusively for documenting any cash or bank outflows. Third are Journal or Non-Cash Vouchers, designed to capture transactions that do not immediately involve cash movements, such as depreciation, credit purchases, and rectification entries.

questions.text_english: State the steps to create a 'Pie Chart' using Excel.

key_points: Organize the data in a single column or row with corresponding labels
Select the entire data range including the labels
Navigate to the 'Insert' tab on the ribbon menu
Locate the 'Charts' group and click on the 'Insert Pie or Doughnut Chart' icon
Select the preferred 2D or 3D Pie Chart style from the drop-down menu
Format the generated chart using 'Chart Design' and 'Format' tabs

questions.solution: To systematically create a Pie Chart using Microsoft Excel, begin by clearly organizing the relevant data into a single column or row, ensuring that each data point has a corresponding text label directly adjacent to it. Next, click and drag to select this entire data range, including both the numerical values and the labels. Then, navigate to the 'Insert' tab located on the top ribbon menu. Within the 'Charts' group, locate and click the specific icon labeled 'Insert Pie or Doughnut Chart'. A drop-down menu will appear, from which you can select the desired visual style, such as a standard 2D Pie or a 3D Pie. Excel will instantly generate the chart on the worksheet. Finally, utilize the 'Chart Design' and 'Format' contextual tabs that appear to customize elements like chart titles, data labels, and color schemes to finalize the presentation.
